01455.overview_and_main_message: This line chart shows the evolution of sales over time, from 2014 to 2025, for three regions: North, Central, and South. Its purpose is to reveal how sales change by period and whether there is a seasonal or cyclical pattern. The main message is that sales decline steadily in all three regions across the whole period, with no repeating seasonal cycle. South remains the highest-selling region throughout, Central stays in the middle, and North is consistently the lowest.
01455.chart_structure: The chart is a multi-series line chart. It represents sales values for three regional series—North, Central, and South—measured over time. The X axis shows the period, using yearly categories from 2014 through 2025. The Y axis shows sales in M€, ranging from 19.6 M€ to 104.0 M€.
01455.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: All three regional series show a clear downward trend over the full period. Sales decrease almost continuously year after year, indicating sustained decline rather than fluctuation around a stable level. The ranking between regions does not change: South has the highest sales in every year, Central is always second, and North remains lowest. This makes the regional differences stable even while all three decline. There is no evidence of seasonality or cyclical recovery. Instead of repeated ups and downs, the chart shows a long-term contraction. The average across the three regions also falls markedly, from about 91.6 M€ in 2014 to about 30.7 M€ in 2025.
01455.essential_key_details: The overall maximum value in the chart is 104.0 M€, reached by South in 2014. The overall minimum is 19.6 M€, reached by North in 2025. Across all 36 values, the overall average is about 62.6 M€. By region, average sales are highest in South at about 74.5 M€, followed by Central at about 62.1 M€, and North at about 51.1 M€. Each region falls substantially from its starting point to its ending point: North declines from 79.3 to 19.6 M€, Central from 91.6 to 29.5 M€, and South from 104.0 to 43.1 M€. These endpoints confirm the chart’s central message of broad, persistent sales decline across all regions.

01524.overview_and_main_message: This chart is a multi-series line chart showing the evolution of three climate-related greenhouse gases by period from 2002 to 2025, measured in ktCO₂e. The main message is a clear regime change around 2014: all three series move from relatively stable lower levels during 2002–2013 to a distinctly higher plateau from 2014 onward. Across the whole period, nitrous oxide remains the highest series, methane stays in the middle, and CO₂ is consistently the lowest.
01524.chart_structure: The chart type is a line chart with three time series: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide. The horizontal axis represents Period, with yearly categories from 2002 to 2025. The vertical axis represents values in ktCO₂e, ranging from 37.4 to 79.1. Each line tracks one gas over time: CO₂ varies between 37.4 and 64.1 ktCO₂e, Methane between 44.5 and 72.1, and Nitrous oxide between 51.5 and 79.1.
01524.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The most important pattern is the abrupt upward shift beginning in 2014 for all three gases. Before 2014, yearly values are relatively steady and much lower: CO₂ stays roughly around the high 30s to low 40s, Methane around the mid-40s, and Nitrous oxide around the low- to mid-50s. From 2014 onward, all three jump to a much higher band and remain there. A second pattern is the stable ranking between series throughout the timeline. Nitrous oxide is always the highest, Methane is always second, and CO₂ is always the lowest. This means differences between gases are persistent even as all three rise together after 2014. A third pattern is that the post-2014 period shows high values with only moderate year-to-year fluctuation rather than a continuous upward climb. After the jump, each series oscillates within a fairly narrow higher range, suggesting a new sustained level rather than temporary spikes.
01524.essential_key_details: The overall minimum in the chart is 37.4 ktCO₂e for CO₂ in 2011, and the overall maximum is 79.1 ktCO₂e for Nitrous oxide in 2023. The overall average across all values is 58.125 ktCO₂e. By series, average values are 50.87 ktCO₂e for CO₂, 58.4 for Methane, and 65.10 for Nitrous oxide. CO₂ reaches its maximum at 64.1 in 2024 and has a minimum of 37.4 in 2011. Methane reaches its maximum at 72.1 in 2015 and its minimum at 44.5 in 2012. Nitrous oxide reaches its maximum at 79.1 in 2023 and its minimum at 51.5 in 2011. Looking at the shift by year, the average across the three gases is about 46.17 ktCO₂e in both 2002 and 2013, then rises sharply to 70.67 in 2014. The highest yearly average occurs in 2023 at 71.2 ktCO₂e. This confirms that the chart’s central message is not a gradual long-term increase, but a marked step change to a higher level starting in 2014.

Across the whole period, nitrous oxide remains the highest series, methane stays in the middle, and CO₂ is consistently the lowest. The chart type is a line chart with three time series: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide. The horizontal axis represents Period, with yearly categories from 2002 to 2025. The vertical axis represents values in ktCO₂e, ranging from 37.4 to 79.1. Each line tracks one gas over time: CO₂ varies between 37.4 and 64.1 ktCO₂e, Methane between 44.5 and 72.1, and Nitrous oxide between 51.5 and 79.1. The most important pattern is the abrupt upward shift beginning in 2014 for all three gases. Before 2014, yearly values are relatively steady and much lower: CO₂ stays roughly around the high 30s to low 40s, Methane around the mid-40s, and Nitrous oxide around the low- to mid-50s. From 2014 onward, all three jump to a much higher band and remain there. A second pattern is the stable ranking between series throughout the timeline. Nitrous oxide is always the highest, Methane is always second, and CO₂ is always the lowest. This means differences between gases are persistent even as all three rise together after 2014. A third pattern is that the post-2014 period shows high values with only moderate year-to-year fluctuation rather than a continuous upward climb. After the jump, each series oscillates within a fairly narrow higher range, suggesting a new sustained level rather than temporary spikes. The overall minimum in the chart is 37.4 ktCO₂e for CO₂ in 2011, and the overall maximum is 79.1 ktCO₂e for Nitrous oxide in 2023. The overall average across all values is 58.125 ktCO₂e. By series, average values are 50.87 ktCO₂e for CO₂, 58.4 for Methane, and 65.10 for Nitrous oxide. CO₂ reaches its maximum at 64.1 in 2024 and has a minimum of 37.4 in 2011. Methane reaches its maximum at 72.1 in 2015 and its minimum at 44.5 in 2012. Nitrous oxide reaches its maximum at 79.1 in 2023 and its minimum at 51.5 in 2011. Looking at the shift by year, the average across the three gases is about 46.17 ktCO₂e in both 2002 and 2013, then rises sharply to 70.67 in 2014. The highest yearly average occurs in 2023 at 71.2 ktCO₂e. This confirms that the chart’s central message is not a gradual long-term increase, but a marked step change to a higher level starting in 2014.

01548.overview_and_main_message: This line chart shows the evolution of three climate-related series—CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide—across the periods from 2011 to 2025. Its purpose is to compare how these emissions values change over time and to identify the highest and lowest points. The main message is that all three series fluctuate noticeably from year to year, with Nitrous oxide generally remaining the highest of the three, CO₂ usually the lowest, and no strong overall upward or downward trend across the full period.
01548.chart_structure: The chart is a multi-series line chart. It represents three variables or series: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide. The horizontal axis shows Period, with annual categories running from 2011 to 2025. The vertical axis shows values in ktCO₂e, ranging from 50.4 to 118.7 ktCO₂e. Each year contains one value for each of the three series, allowing comparison both over time within each gas and between gases in the same year.
01548.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: A first clear pattern is that Nitrous oxide is typically the highest series throughout the chart. Its average value is about 91.6 ktCO₂e, compared with 78.6 for Methane and 68.1 for CO₂. It also contains the overall maximum value in the chart. A second pattern is that the chart is highly variable rather than steady. All three series move up and down over time, with repeated peaks and dips instead of a smooth trend. This means the chart communicates volatility more than long-term growth or decline. A third pattern is that some years show relatively close values across all three gases, while others show wide separation. For example, 2014 is comparatively clustered, with all values between 80.8 and 91.7 ktCO₂e, whereas 2021 shows a much wider spread, from 63.7 to 118.7 ktCO₂e.
01548.essential_key_details: The overall average across all values in the chart is about 79.4 ktCO₂e. The highest value in the entire chart is 118.7 ktCO₂e for Nitrous oxide in 2021. Other very high Nitrous oxide values include 118.3 in 2018 and 112.6 in 2016. The lowest value in the entire chart is 50.4 ktCO₂e for CO₂ in 2012; another low CO₂ point is 51.2 in 2020. By series, CO₂ ranges from 50.4 to 92.7 ktCO₂e and averages 68.1. Methane ranges from 63.1 to 100.5 and averages 78.6; its maximum of 100.5 occurs twice, in 2012 and 2022. Nitrous oxide ranges from 68.0 to 118.7 and averages 91.6, making it both the highest on average and the most extreme at the top end. Looking at annual averages across the three gases, 2016 is one of the highest years at 90.2 ktCO₂e, while 2017 is the lowest at about 62.5 ktCO₂e. This reinforces that the chart’s central message is year-to-year fluctuation, with Nitrous oxide usually leading and CO₂ usually trailing.

01626.overview_and_main_message: This line chart shows the evolution of three climate-related greenhouse gas series over the period 2011 to 2025: CO₂, methane, and nitrous oxide, measured in ktCO₂e. Its main message is that all three series follow the same broad pattern: they rise from 2011 to a peak around 2015, then decline steadily to their lowest levels in 2022 or 2023, followed by a modest recovery through 2025. Across the whole period, nitrous oxide remains the highest series, methane stays in the middle, and CO₂ is consistently the lowest.
01626.chart_structure: The chart type is a multi-series line chart. It represents time periods on the X axis and greenhouse gas values on the Y axis. The X axis is labeled Period and includes yearly categories from 2011 to 2025. The Y axis is labeled ktCO₂e and spans values from 50.8 to 117.0 ktCO₂e. There are three series: CO₂, methane, and nitrous oxide. Each series reports one value for each year.
01626.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: All three gases increase during the first part of the period, from 2011 to 2015. Yearly average values across the three gases rise from about 82.9 ktCO₂e in 2011 to about 105.9 ktCO₂e in 2015, the highest annual average in the chart. After 2015, all three series decline for several years. The overall yearly average falls to about 59.0 ktCO₂e in 2022, the lowest annual average, and remains similarly low in 2023 at about 60.6 before turning upward again. The relative ranking does not change over time. Nitrous oxide is always the highest, methane always intermediate, and CO₂ always the lowest. This means the three lines move in parallel rather than crossing, indicating similar timing of increase, decline, and recovery.
01626.essential_key_details: The maximum value in the entire chart is 117.0 ktCO₂e for nitrous oxide in 2015. The minimum value is 50.8 ktCO₂e for CO₂ in 2022. By series, average values over 2011–2025 are 72.8 ktCO₂e for CO₂, 82.9 for methane, and 92.3 for nitrous oxide. Their individual peaks all occur in 2015: CO₂ at 93.8, methane at 107.0, and nitrous oxide at 117.0 ktCO₂e. Their lowest values occur near the end of the decline phase: CO₂ reaches 50.8 in 2022, methane reaches 58.3 in 2022, and nitrous oxide reaches 67.8 in 2022. After that point, each series rises again by 2025, reaching 64.9 for CO₂, 74.3 for methane, and 81.4 ktCO₂e for nitrous oxide. The overall mean across all 45 values in the chart is about 82.6 ktCO₂e.

01710.overview_and_main_message: This line chart shows the evolution of three climate-related emission series across periods from 2015 to 2025: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide, measured in ktCO₂e. Its purpose is to show how these indicators change over time and to help identify the highest and lowest values. The main message is that all three series follow a similar pattern: they rise from 2015 to a peak around 2018, then decline steadily to their lowest levels around 2023 or 2024, followed by a modest rebound in 2025. Throughout the whole period, Nitrous oxide remains the highest of the three series, while CO₂ is consistently the lowest.
01710.chart_structure: The chart type is a multi-series line chart. It represents time on the X axis and emission values on the Y axis. The X axis is labelled Period and contains yearly categories from 2015 through 2025. The Y axis is labelled ktCO₂e and ranges from 78.7 to 181.0 ktCO₂e. The three lines correspond to the series CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide.
01710.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: All three series increase from 2015 to 2018, indicating a shared upward phase. The overall average across all data points also reflects this high period, with yearly means rising from about 128.8 ktCO₂e in 2015 to the highest yearly average of about 168.0 in 2018. After 2018, all series decline markedly through 2023 or 2024. The lowest yearly average occurs in 2023 at about 92.0 ktCO₂e, showing that this is the deepest common downturn across the chart. The relative ranking is stable across the whole time span: Nitrous oxide is always the highest series, Methane stays in the middle, and CO₂ is always the lowest. Their average values over the full period are about 142.0 ktCO₂e for Nitrous oxide, 130.4 for Methane, and 115.9 for CO₂.
01710.essential_key_details: The maximum value in the chart is 181.0 ktCO₂e, reached by Nitrous oxide in 2018. The minimum value is 78.7 ktCO₂e, reached by CO₂ in 2023. By series, CO₂ ranges from 78.7 to 149.7 and averages 115.9 ktCO₂e. Methane ranges from 89.9 to 173.2 and averages 130.4. Nitrous oxide ranges from 107.4 to 181.0 and averages 142.0. A key milestone is 2018, when all three series are at or near their peaks: CO₂ at 149.7, Methane at 173.2, and Nitrous oxide at 181.0. Another key milestone is the trough around 2023 to 2024: CO₂ falls to 78.7 in 2023, Methane reaches its minimum of 89.9 in 2024, and Nitrous oxide reaches its minimum of 107.4 in 2023. In 2025, each series rises again to 98.4 for CO₂, 109.0 for Methane, and 120.7 for Nitrous oxide, indicating a partial recovery after the decline.

Across all 33 plotted values, the overall average is about 148.2 ktCO₂e. The key milestones are therefore the two sudden valleys in Nitrous oxide in 2019 and 2024; all other years and both other series remain unchanged.

01807.overview_and_main_message: This chart shows the evolution of sales by period from 2016 to 2025 for three regions: North, Central, and South. It is intended to reveal how sales change over time and whether there is a cyclical or seasonal pattern. The main message is that all three regions follow a very similar trajectory: sales rise from 2016 to a peak around 2018–2019, then decline steadily through 2024, followed by a modest recovery in 2025. South remains the strongest-performing region throughout, Central stays in the middle, and North is consistently the lowest.
01807.chart_structure: The chart is a multi-series line chart with markers. It compares sales over time across three series: North, Central, and South. The X axis represents Period, with yearly categories from 2016 to 2025. The Y axis represents sales in M€, ranging from 22.3 M€ to 108.9 M€. Each line corresponds to one region, showing how its sales value changes year by year across the same ten periods.
01807.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: All three regions share the same broad pattern: growth from 2016 until 2018 or 2019, then a prolonged downturn from 2020 to 2024, and finally a partial rebound in 2025. This repeated rise-and-fall structure is the clearest sign of a common temporal pattern across the series. South records the highest sales in every year, Central is always second, and North is always lowest. The ranking never changes, so differences between regions are stable even while all three move up and down together. The strongest years overall are 2018 and 2019, when the average across regions reaches about 91.2 M€ and 92.2 M€ respectively. The weakest period is 2024, when the cross-region average falls to 32.9 M€, before improving to 44.1 M€ in 2025.
01807.essential_key_details: Across the whole chart, the maximum value is 108.9 M€, reached by South in 2019. The minimum value is 22.3 M€, reached by North in 2024. The overall average across all values is about 62.9 M€. By region, average sales are highest in South at 74.0 M€, followed by Central at 62.1 M€, and North at 52.8 M€. The regional peaks are 80.9 M€ for North in 2018, 88.8 M€ for Central in 2019, and 108.9 M€ for South in 2019. The regional minimums occur late in the period: 22.3 M€ for North in 2024, 34.5 M€ for Central in 2024, and 41.9 M€ for South in 2024. A key milestone is the turning point after 2019: average sales across regions drop from 92.2 M€ in 2019 to 80.6 M€ in 2020, continue down to 34.5 M€ in 2023 and 32.9 M€ in 2024, then recover slightly in 2025.

01810.overview_and_main_message: This chart shows the evolution of three climate-related emission series over time: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide, measured from 2006 to 2025 in ktCO₂e. The main message is a clear regime change around 2016: all three series stay relatively stable at lower levels from 2006 to 2015, then jump sharply upward and remain on a higher plateau through 2025. Across the whole period, Nitrous oxide is consistently the highest series, Methane stays in the middle, and CO₂ remains the lowest.
01810.chart_structure: The chart is a multi-series line chart with markers. It represents three variables by period: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide. The X axis shows Period, with yearly categories from 2006 to 2025. The Y axis shows values in ktCO₂e, ranging from 38.9 to 78.6. Each line traces the yearly values of one gas across the 20 periods, allowing comparison of both change over time and differences between the three series.
01810.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The most important pattern is the abrupt upward shift in 2016 for all three gases. Before 2016, annual values cluster in lower bands: CO₂ is roughly around 39 to 42, Methane around 45 to 49, and Nitrous oxide around 51 to 55. From 2016 onward, the series move to much higher bands: CO₂ mostly around 58 to 61, Methane around 67 to 71, and Nitrous oxide around 76 to 79. A second pattern is the stable ranking between series throughout the entire chart. Nitrous oxide is always highest, Methane is always intermediate, and CO₂ is always lowest, both before and after the shift. A third pattern is that, after the jump in 2016, values fluctuate only modestly within their new higher ranges rather than continuing to rise strongly year after year. This suggests a level shift followed by relative stabilization.
01810.essential_key_details: The overall minimum value in the chart is 38.9 ktCO₂e for CO₂ in 2008. The overall maximum is 78.6 ktCO₂e for Nitrous oxide in 2025. Average values by series reinforce the hierarchy: CO₂ has a mean of 50.13 ktCO₂e, Methane 57.965 ktCO₂e, and Nitrous oxide 65.345 ktCO₂e. The overall average across all data points is 57.813 ktCO₂e. Key milestones include 2015 to 2016, where each series rises sharply: CO₂ increases from 42.1 to 58.7, Methane from 48.4 to 71.2, and Nitrous oxide from 51.1 to 78.3. By the end of the period in 2025, values remain close to this elevated regime: CO₂ is 58.1, Methane 69.8, and Nitrous oxide 78.6 ktCO₂e.

Its purpose is to compare how these three series change by period and to identify their highest and lowest values. The main message is that all three series fluctuate noticeably from year to year rather than following a smooth long-term rise or decline, with Nitrous oxide generally having the highest values, CO₂ the lowest overall, and Methane lying between them.
01834.chart_structure: The chart is a multi-series line chart with markers. It represents time periods on the X axis and emission values on the Y axis. The X axis is labeled Period and contains annual categories from 2011 through 2025. The Y axis is labeled ktCO₂e and ranges from 55.2 to 112.0 ktCO₂e. There are three lines, one for each series: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide. Each value shows the amount for that gas in a given year.
01834.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The first important pattern is the overall ranking of the three series. Nitrous oxide is usually the highest series and has the highest average value, about 90.3 ktCO₂e. Methane is next, averaging about 85.2 ktCO₂e. CO₂ is generally lowest, with an average of about 75.7 ktCO₂e. The second pattern is strong year-to-year variability across all series. CO₂ drops sharply from 92.3 in 2011 to 57.4 in 2012, rises again to 87.8 in 2013, and later returns to high values around 89.0 to 90.0 in 2018 to 2020. Methane also swings substantially, moving from 60.6 in 2014 to 106.7 in 2018, then down to 68.2 in 2024. Nitrous oxide alternates between high peaks and lower years, such as 110.7 in 2014, 71.1 in 2018, and 112.0 in 2022. The third pattern is that some years show convergence while others show wide separation between gases. In 2013 and 2025 the three values are relatively close to one another, indicating limited spread across gases in those years. By contrast, 2012 and 2014 show much larger differences between the lowest and highest series.
01834.essential_key_details: Across all data points, the maximum value in the chart is 112.0 ktCO₂e for Nitrous oxide in 2022. The minimum value is 55.2 ktCO₂e for CO₂ in 2016. Methane ranges from 60.6 to 106.7 ktCO₂e and shows the widest spread among its values. Nitrous oxide ranges from 71.1 to 112.0 ktCO₂e and has both the highest average and the chart’s overall peak. Looking at periods as a whole, 2022 has the highest average across the three gases, about 92.9 ktCO₂e, while 2016 has the lowest period average, about 74.7 ktCO₂e. The final year, 2025, stands out because all three series cluster tightly between 72.3 and 77.3 ktCO₂e, making it one of the most uniform years in the chart.

01843.overview_and_main_message: This chart shows the evolution of sales by period across three regions—North, Central, and South—with the aim of revealing whether sales follow a seasonal pattern over the four quarters. The main message is a clear and consistent upward trend from Q1 to Q4 in all three regions, indicating strong growth through the year rather than fluctuation. South records the highest sales overall, while North starts from a much lower level and remains the lowest series despite substantial growth.
01843.chart_structure: This is a multi-series line chart with markers. It compares sales values over time for three series: North, Central, and South. The X axis represents Period and is divided into four quarterly categories: Q1, Q2, Q3, and Q4. The Y axis represents sales in M€, with values ranging from 22.5 M€ to 189.0 M€. Each line corresponds to one region: North has sales of 22.5, 67.6, 113.8, and 149.4 M€ from Q1 to Q4. Central has sales of 59.3, 88.6, 125.7, and 158.0 M€. South has sales of 58.7, 98.7, 152.1, and 189.0 M€.
01843.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: All three regions increase steadily quarter by quarter, so the dominant pattern is continuous growth across the year. There are no declines or reversals in any series. South is the strongest performer overall. It is already close to Central in Q1, moves ahead in Q2, and extends that lead by Q3 and Q4, finishing at the highest value in the chart. North remains the weakest series throughout, beginning far below the other two regions in Q1. Even though it grows strongly over time, it does not catch up to Central or South. Central stays between North and South in every quarter.
01843.essential_key_details: The maximum value in the chart is 189.0 M€, reached by South in Q4. The minimum value is 22.5 M€, recorded by North in Q1. The overall average across all 12 data points is 106.95 M€. Average sales also rise strongly by quarter, reinforcing the year-long growth pattern: 46.83 M€ in Q1, 84.97 M€ in Q2, 130.53 M€ in Q3, and 165.47 M€ in Q4. By region, average sales are 88.33 M€ for North, 107.9 M€ for Central, and 124.63 M€ for South, confirming that South leads overall and North trails. The key milestone is the consistent progression toward peak sales in Q4 for every region, which is the clearest evidence of a seasonal build-up through the year.

The main message is a clear and consistent decline in all three series throughout the whole period, indicating broad reductions in emissions measured in ktCO₂e.
01846.chart_structure: The chart is a multi-series line chart with markers. It compares three variables: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide. The horizontal axis represents Period, with eight yearly categories from 2018 to 2025. The vertical axis represents emissions in ktCO₂e, ranging from 101.5 to 214.4 ktCO₂e. Each line tracks one gas over time, allowing comparison of their levels and their rate of decline across the same periods.
01846.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: All three series decrease every year without interruption from 2018 to 2025, so the overall pattern is a steady downward trend across the full time span. Nitrous oxide remains the highest series in every year, while CO₂ is the lowest in most years. Methane starts above CO₂ and remains above it until the final year, when Methane falls below CO₂ in 2025. Methane shows the largest overall drop, falling from 206.6 to 101.5 ktCO₂e, while CO₂ declines from 171.5 to 106.5 and Nitrous oxide from 214.4 to 121.8. This means Methane changes the most in absolute terms, and by the end of the period the three series are closer together than at the start.
01846.essential_key_details: The maximum value in the chart is 214.4 ktCO₂e for Nitrous oxide in 2018. The minimum value is 101.5 ktCO₂e for Methane in 2025. Average values by series are 139.7 for CO₂, 153.6 for Methane, and 168.3 for Nitrous oxide, confirming that Nitrous oxide is generally highest over the period. A useful milestone is the change in yearly average across all three gases: it falls from 197.5 ktCO₂e in 2018 to 109.9 ktCO₂e in 2025, summarising the chart’s central message of sustained decline over time.

01891.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The first clear pattern is a shared time trend across all regions. Sales increase from 2012 to the mid-2010s, reaching their highest levels around 2015 or 2016, then fall year after year until the early 2020s, before turning upward again in the final two years. The second pattern is the consistent ranking of regions. South has the highest sales in every year, Central is always in the middle, and North is always the lowest. The rebound does not return sales to earlier peak levels.

Their low points occur in the early 2020s: North falls to 15.0 M€ in 2022, Central to 16.5 M€ in 2023, and South to 23.6 M€ in both 2022 and 2023. 01936.overview_and_main_message: This chart shows the evolution of three climate-related greenhouse gas series—CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide—across the periods from 2015 to 2025. Its main message is that all three series remain relatively stable at lower levels from 2015 to 2019, then shift sharply upward in 2020 and stay at this higher regime through 2025. Throughout the whole period, Nitrous oxide is generally the highest series, CO₂ the lowest, and Methane remains in between.
01936.chart_structure: This is a multi-series line chart with markers. It compares three variables: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide. The X axis represents Period, with annual categories from 2015 to 2025. The Y axis represents values in ktCO₂e, ranging from 123.5 to 194.1 ktCO₂e. Each line tracks one gas over time, allowing comparison of both year-to-year change and differences between the three gases.
01936.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The dominant pattern is a clear regime change between 2019 and 2020. Before 2020, values for all three gases are notably lower: CO₂ stays around 123.5 to 127.6, Methane around 140.5 to 146.0, and Nitrous oxide around 155.6 to 159.9. From 2020 onward, all three jump to much higher levels and remain elevated. A second important pattern is the persistent ranking of the series. Nitrous oxide is highest in every year, CO₂ is lowest in every year, and Methane always lies between them. This means the chart communicates not only growth over time but also a stable ordering among the three gases. A third pattern is that, after the jump in 2020, the series fluctuate only modestly within their new higher band rather than continuing to rise steadily. The post-2020 averages by year stay close to 180 to 183 ktCO₂e overall, showing stabilization at a higher level rather than ongoing acceleration.
01936.essential_key_details: The overall minimum value in the chart is 123.5 ktCO₂e for CO₂ in 2015. The overall maximum is 194.1 ktCO₂e for Nitrous oxide in 2020. Average values by series confirm the long-term ranking: CO₂ averages 150.1 ktCO₂e, Methane 163.0 ktCO₂e, and Nitrous oxide 176.0 ktCO₂e. The overall average across all data points is 163.0 ktCO₂e. The year-level averages highlight the structural break: the mean across the three gases is about 140.8 to 143.8 ktCO₂e from 2015 to 2019, then rises to 181.4 ktCO₂e in 2020 and remains high, reaching its highest annual mean in 2022 at 182.5 ktCO₂e. This makes 2020 the key turning point in the chart.

This indicates a shared seasonal pattern rather than independent movement. Nitrous oxide remains above the other two series throughout the entire period, with Methane in the middle and CO₂ lowest. Their average values confirm this ordering: Nitrous oxide averages 231.65 ktCO₂e, Methane 214.53 ktCO₂e, and CO₂ 199.2 ktCO₂e. 02151.overview_and_main_message: This chart shows the evolution of sales over time from 2015 to 2025 for three regions: North, Central, and South. It is intended to reveal whether sales follow a seasonal or cyclical pattern across periods. The main message is that sales fluctuate strongly from year to year rather than following a smooth common cycle, with South consistently recording the highest sales overall, North the lowest, and Central in between. Across all data points, the overall average is about 63.3 M€.
02151.chart_structure: The chart is a stacked line chart with three time series. It represents sales values in millions of euros for the regions North, Central, and South. The X-axis shows the period as annual categories from 2015 through 2025. The Y-axis shows sales in M€, ranging from 24.7 M€ to 98.5 M€.
02151.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The clearest comparison is between regions. South is generally the strongest series throughout the period, with an average of about 77.1 M€, compared with 64.2 M€ for Central and 48.8 M€ for North. North remains the weakest series overall. A second important pattern is the high variability over time. Sales do not move in a steady direction and instead rise and fall noticeably across years. This is visible both within individual regions and in the yearly combined averages: the mean across regions falls to about 41.9 M€ in 2018, then rises to around 74.7 M€ in 2020, drops again, and reaches about 73.7 M€ in 2025. A third notable pattern is that 2019 is the most similar year across the three regions, with values tightly grouped between 59.8 M€ and 65.2 M€, while other years show much wider gaps. In contrast, 2022 has the widest spread between regions, indicating especially uneven sales performance that year.
02151.essential_key_details: The maximum value in the chart is 98.5 M€, reached by South in 2022. The minimum value is 24.7 M€, recorded by North in 2015. By series, North ranges from 24.7 M€ to 77.0 M€ and averages 48.8 M€; Central ranges from 38.7 M€ to 85.8 M€ and averages 64.2 M€; South ranges from 48.6 M€ to 98.5 M€ and averages 77.1 M€. Looking at the average across the three regions for each year, the lowest year is 2018 at about 41.9 M€, and the highest year is 2020 at about 74.7 M€, closely followed by 2016 at 74.0 M€ and 2025 at 73.7 M€. These milestones reinforce the chart’s message of substantial year-to-year fluctuation rather than a stable seasonal rhythm.

02163.overview_and_main_message: This chart shows the evolution of sales by period from 2018 to 2025 for three regions: North, Central, and South. The main message is a clear and sustained decline in sales across all regions over time, with South consistently recording the highest sales, North the lowest, and no evident seasonal or cyclical rebound during the period.

The gap between regions becomes more pronounced over time. 02178.overview_and_main_message: This chart is a stacked line chart showing the evolution of three climate-related series—CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide—across the periods from 2017 to 2025, measured in ktCO₂e. The main message is that Nitrous oxide remains completely stable at the highest level throughout the whole period, while CO₂ and Methane are mostly stable but experience brief drops, creating a clear temporary valley around 2020 to 2023, especially in 2022.
02178.chart_structure: The chart type is a stacked line chart with three series. It represents climate-related values for CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide over time. The X-axis shows the period as yearly categories from 2017 through 2025. The Y-axis shows values in ktCO₂e, ranging from 114.7 to 189.9. Each series tracks one gas over the same nine periods: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide.
02178.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The most consistent pattern is the complete stability of Nitrous oxide. It stays at 189.9 ktCO₂e in every year, making it both the highest series and the overall maximum value in the chart. CO₂ is stable at 159.9 ktCO₂e for most years, but it drops to 114.7 in 2022 and remains at 114.7 in 2023 before returning to 159.9 in 2024 and 2025. This creates the deepest and most prolonged dip among the three series. Methane is generally stable at 177.8 ktCO₂e, but it falls to 126.1 in 2020 and again in 2022. Unlike CO₂, these declines are isolated interruptions rather than a two-year low. Across most of the period, Methane stays between CO₂ and Nitrous oxide.

The highest average period level is 175.87 ktCO₂e, occurring in 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2024, and 2025.

02243.overview_and_main_message: This chart shows the evolution of sales over time, from 2009 to 2025, for three regions: North, Central, and South. Its main message is a broad and sustained decline in sales across all regions over the whole period, with no clear seasonal or cyclical pattern. South consistently has the highest sales, Central remains in the middle, and North stays lowest, but all three move downward.
02243.chart_structure: The chart is a multi-series line chart with markers, specifically a stacked line chart, used to show changes in sales over time for several regions. The variables represented are period and sales value, with a separate series for each region: North, Central, and South. The X axis represents Period and contains yearly categories from 2009 through 2025. The Y axis represents sales in M€, ranging from 10.9 M€ to 45.7 M€.
02243.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: All three regional series decline substantially from the beginning to the end of the period. North falls from 30.8 M€ in 2009 to 10.9 M€ in 2025, Central from 37.5 M€ to 12.7 M€, and South from 45.7 M€ to 15.3 M€. South is consistently the highest-selling region in every year, Central is always between South and North, and North is always the lowest. The ranking never changes, so the gaps narrow over time but there is no crossover between regions. The overall yearly average across the three regions also drops steadily, from 38.0 M€ in 2009 and 37.9 M€ in 2010 to 13.0 M€ in 2025. This reinforces that the chart communicates a general downward market trend rather than short-term fluctuations.
02243.essential_key_details: The maximum value in the chart is 45.7 M€, recorded by South in 2009. The minimum value is 10.9 M€, recorded by North in 2025. By series average, South has the highest mean sales at about 30.9 M€, Central averages 26.1 M€, and North averages 20.9 M€. A key milestone is the end of the series in 2025, when all regions reach their lowest levels: North 10.9 M€, Central 12.7 M€, and South 15.3 M€. Another useful reference point is 2019 to 2020, when the combined yearly mean declines from 22.2 M€ to 20.9 M€, continuing the longer downward trajectory rather than reversing it.

02303.overview_and_main_message: This chart shows the evolution of sales over time from 2017 to 2025 for three regions: North, Central, and South. The main message is consistent growth across all regions, with no declines in any series. 02303.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: All three regions show a clear upward trend over the full period, indicating sustained sales growth rather than a cyclical or seasonal pattern. The average across all values is about 63.34 M€, and the yearly mean rises steadily from 30.67 M€ in 2017 to 97.0 M€ in 2025. South starts well ahead in 2017 at 46.0 M€, compared with 25.6 M€ for Central and 20.4 M€ for North. It remains the highest series through most years, although the gap narrows over time as Central grows faster. By 2025, Central and South converge at very similar levels, with Central at 102.7 M€ and South at 103.0 M€, while North reaches 85.3 M€. This indicates that Central experiences the strongest overall rise, even though South keeps the top final value.

02383.overview_and_main_message: This chart is a 100% stacked line chart showing the evolution of climate-related percentage contributions by period from 2008 to 2025. It compares three components—CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide—within each year, where the three values always sum to 100%. The main message is that the relative contributions remain broadly balanced over time, usually close to one third each, but with some notable shifts in dominance: Methane reaches the highest single share in 2016, CO₂ peaks in 2020, and Nitrous oxide is strongest in 2017. Overall, there is no strong long-term upward or downward trend across the full period.

Because this is a 100% stacked chart, each year represents a complete distribution of 100% split among the three series.
02383.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: A first important pattern is the general balance among the three series. This means no series consistently dominates the others over time. A second pattern is the presence of specific peaks and dips rather than a sustained trend. Methane reaches the chart’s overall maximum at 41.3% in 2016, then falls to 27.5% in 2020 and to its own minimum of 26.5% in 2025. CO₂ has the lowest value in the entire chart at 24.5% in 2011, but later rises sharply to 41.1% in 2020. Nitrous oxide also shows clear variation, peaking at 40.3% in 2017. A third pattern is that some years are much more evenly distributed than others. For example, 2023 is especially balanced, with all three contributions close together between 31.4% and 34.5%. By contrast, years such as 2011, 2016, 2017, and 2020 show wider gaps between the highest and lowest series, indicating stronger shifts in which component leads.

02389.overview_and_main_message: This chart is a 100% stacked line chart titled “Evolution of climate by period (02389).” Its purpose is to show how the percentage contribution of three climate-related components—CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide—changes across periods from 2011 to 2025. The main message is that the three components share the total quite evenly in most years, usually around one third each, but leadership shifts from year to year: CO₂ is most often the largest contributor overall, Methane varies the most, and Nitrous oxide becomes comparatively stronger in the later years.
02389.chart_structure: The chart type is a 100% stacked line chart. It represents three series: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide. The X axis shows Period, with yearly categories from 2011 through 2025. The Y axis shows percentage contribution, ranging from 0% to 100%. Because the chart is 100% stacked, the three values for each year add up to 100%, so the chart compares each gas’s share of the yearly total rather than absolute amounts.
02389.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: A first important pattern is the overall balance among the three gases. In every year, each contribution stays within a relatively narrow band of about 26.5% to 39.5%, so no single gas dominates the whole period. The overall average across all plotted values is 33.33%, which reflects this near-even split. A second pattern is that CO₂ has the highest average share across the full period. Its mean contribution is 34.91%, compared with 32.37% for Methane and 32.73% for Nitrous oxide. CO₂ reaches the highest value in the entire chart, 39.5% in 2012, although it also drops to 29.0% in 2013, showing that its lead is not constant. A third pattern is the contrast in variability and timing between Methane and Nitrous oxide. Methane is the most volatile series, ranging from 26.5% to 38.9%; it peaks strongly in 2013 and is lowest in 2012. Nitrous oxide is somewhat steadier overall and shows a slight upward tendency across the period, with notable highs in 2021 at 37.7% and 2023 at 37.6%, making it one of the strongest contributors in the later years.
02389.essential_key_details: The maximum value in the chart is 39.5%, for CO₂ in 2012. The minimum value is 26.5%, for Methane in 2012. By series, CO₂ ranges from 29.0% to 39.5% and has the highest average at 34.91%. Methane ranges from 26.5% to 38.9% and has the lowest average at 32.37%, while also showing the widest range, 12.4 percentage points. Nitrous oxide ranges from 27.5% to 37.7% and averages 32.73%. Two years stand out for how evenly the total is split: 2014, when values range only from 32.4% to 33.9%, and especially 2022, when all three series are almost equal, between 32.8% and 33.8%. These years contrast with 2012, which shows the widest spread within a year, from 26.5% to 39.5%.

02413.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: A first important pattern is overall balance. 02735.overview_and_main_message: This chart is a doughnut chart with two rings comparing the category composition of sales for Actual versus Target. Its purpose is to show how total sales are distributed across five channels and whether the current composition differs from the target composition. The main message is that sales are overwhelmingly concentrated in Physical store in both series, at about 88% of sales, while all other channels each contribute less than 4%. Actual and Target are therefore very similar, with only small differences in the smaller channels.
02735.chart_structure: The chart type is a multi-ring doughnut chart, a part-to-whole chart used here to compare two series: Actual and Target. Each ring represents one series, and each ring is divided into the same five sales categories. The variables represented are sales category and percentage of sales. The categories are Physical store, E-commerce, Distributor, Marketplace, and Phone channel. The quantitative measure is % of sales. The X axis corresponds to Category, running through the five named categories. The Y axis corresponds to % of sales, with values ranging from 1.9 to 88.2 percent. Because this is a doughnut chart, the key reading task is comparing the share of each category within each series rather than following a continuous scale.
02735.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The dominant pattern is the extreme concentration in Physical store. It accounts for 88.1% of Actual sales and 88.2% of Target sales, making it by far the largest component in both rings and the clear driver of the overall composition. A second pattern is that the remaining channels are all minor contributors and are close to one another. E-commerce is the largest of these smaller categories at 3.8% in Actual and 3.9% in Target. Distributor and Marketplace are both around 3%, while Phone channel is the smallest at 1.9% in both series. A third pattern is that Actual and Target are almost the same overall, with only slight shifts among the smaller channels. Relative to Target, Actual is slightly higher for Distributor by 0.6 percentage points, slightly lower for Marketplace by 0.4 points, slightly lower for E-commerce by 0.1 point, and unchanged for Phone channel. These differences do not alter the overall picture of strong dependence on Physical store.
02735.essential_key_details: The maximum value in the chart is Physical store in Target at 88.2%, closely followed by Physical store in Actual at 88.1%. The minimum value is Phone channel at 1.9% in both series. Each series sums to 100% and has an average category share of 20.0%, but this average is not representative of the typical category because one category is overwhelmingly dominant. The median category share is much lower: 3.5% for Actual, 3.1% for Target, and 3.3% overall. This contrast between the 20.0% average and the roughly 3% median reinforces that most categories are small and that the composition is highly skewed toward Physical store. Across categories, the average shares are 88.15% for Physical store, 3.85% for E-commerce, 3.2% for Distributor, 2.9% for Marketplace, and 1.9% for Phone channel. These figures summarise the intended composition and confirm that only Physical store holds a major share of sales.

02930.overview_and_main_message: This chart is an area chart showing the evolution of three climate-related emission series over time: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide. Its purpose is to show how these values change by period from 2001 to 2025, measured in ktCO₂e. The main message is a clear long-term decline across all three gases. Nitrous oxide remains the highest series throughout, CO₂ becomes the lowest, and the overall level across the three series falls substantially over the period.
02930.chart_structure: The chart type is a multi-series area chart with three series: CO₂, Methane, and Nitrous oxide. The horizontal axis represents Period, using yearly categories from 2001 to 2025. The vertical axis represents emissions in ktCO₂e, with values ranging from 22.3 to 74.6 ktCO₂e. Each year contains one value for each of the three gases, allowing comparison over time and between series.
02930.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: All three series show a sustained downward trend from the beginning to the end of the period, despite some short-lived increases. CO₂ falls from 69.2 in 2001 to 22.3 in 2025, Methane from 71.1 to 33.5, and Nitrous oxide from 74.6 to 42.8. Nitrous oxide is consistently the largest of the three series in every year. Methane stays between Nitrous oxide and CO₂ for nearly the entire period, while CO₂ declines the most sharply and ends far below the others. The average across the three gases also declines strongly over time. The mean value for a year drops from 71.6 ktCO₂e in 2001 to 32.9 ktCO₂e in 2025, showing that the reduction is broad-based rather than limited to a single series.
02930.essential_key_details: The maximum value in the chart is 74.6 ktCO₂e for Nitrous oxide in 2001. The minimum value is 22.3 ktCO₂e for CO₂ in 2025. Across all 75 observations, the overall average is 52.86 ktCO₂e. By series, average values are 46.29 for CO₂, 52.96 for Methane, and 59.33 for Nitrous oxide, confirming that Nitrous oxide is typically highest and CO₂ lowest. The final year, 2025, has the lowest combined annual total at 98.6 and the lowest annual mean at 32.87, while 2001 has the highest combined total at 214.9 and the highest annual mean at 71.63. There are a few temporary reversals within the broader decline, such as small increases in CO₂ in 2005, 2015, and 2021; in Methane in 2003, 2006, 2009, 2012, 2015, 2019, and 2021; and in Nitrous oxide in 2007, 2015, 2020, and 2023. These do not change the overall interpretation of steady long-term reduction.

03016.chart_structure: The chart type is a stacked area chart. It represents energy values for four series—Baseload, Renewable, Support, and Others—accumulated by period. The X axis shows Period, with yearly categories from 2011 through 2025. 03016.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The first major pattern is a consistent decline in every series over the full period. Baseload drops from 929.5 GWh in 2011 to 154.2 GWh in 2025, Renewable from 1023.6 to 305.1, Support from 1069.1 to 457.2, and Others from 1260.0 to 522.8. A second key pattern is that Others remains the largest contributor throughout, while Baseload is generally the smallest and also ends at the lowest level. Most series continue downward year after year, but there are small interruptions near the end: Others rises from 552.8 in 2023 to 575.4 in 2024 before falling again, and Baseload rises slightly from 145.2 in 2024 to 154.2 in 2025. Across all 60 values in the chart, the overall average is 710.5 GWh. Looking at the combined yearly totals, the sum across all four series falls from 4282.2 GWh in 2011 to 1439.3 GWh in 2025, with the lowest yearly total occurring in 2025. This confirms that the central takeaway of the chart is a strong long-term contraction in energy across all components.

03088.overview_and_main_message: This chart is a 100% stacked area chart showing the evolution of sales composition by period from 1997 to 2025. It compares how total sales are divided each year among five series: North, Central, South, Others, and Residual. The main message is that the sales mix remains broadly balanced over time, with each series usually contributing around one fifth of total sales. There is no strong long-term shift toward a single series; instead, leadership changes from year to year, with occasional peaks and dips.
03088.chart_structure: The chart type is a 100% stacked area chart. It represents the percentage share of total sales contributed by five series across time. The X axis represents Period, with yearly categories from 1997 through 2025. The Y axis represents % of sales, ranging from 0 to 100. Because the chart is stacked to 100%, each year sums to 100% and the values indicate relative contribution rather than absolute sales volume. The five series are North, Central, South, Others, and Residual. Their values are generally close to 20% each in most years.
03088.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The first key pattern is overall stability in the sales distribution. Across the full period, the global average is 20.0%, and each series has a mean very close to that level: Others is lowest at about 19.5%, North about 19.9%, Central about 20.1%, Residual about 20.3%, and South highest at about 20.3%. This indicates a consistently balanced market split. The second pattern is moderate year-to-year variation without a sustained trend. Some years are especially even, such as 2006, when all series fall between 19.0% and 21.1%. Other years show wider separation, such as 2014 and 2024, when one or two series rise well above 24% while another falls near 16% or lower. The third pattern is that different series take turns having the highest share. South reaches high points in 1997, 2010, 2012, and 2013; Others leads strongly in 2014 and 2020; Residual is strongest in 2008, 2017, and 2018; and Central peaks in 2024. No single series dominates throughout the timeline.
03088.essential_key_details: The maximum value in the chart is 25.5%, reached by Others in 2014. The minimum value is 14.9%, reached by South in 1999. Looking at averages across all years, South has the highest mean share at 20.27%, closely followed by Residual at 20.25% and Central at 20.09%, while Others has the lowest mean at 19.53%. Important milestones include 2006 as the most even year, with a very narrow spread from 19.0% to 21.1%, and 2024 as one of the most uneven years, ranging from 15.4% for Residual to 24.3% for Central. Overall, the chart communicates that sales shares fluctuate within a relatively narrow band around 20%, with short-term shifts in which region or category contributes the largest portion.

03094.overview_and_main_message: This chart is a 100% stacked area chart showing the evolution of climate-related composition by period from 2008 to 2025. Its purpose is to compare how the percentage contribution of four components—CO₂, Methane, Nitrous oxide, and Others—changes over time within a total that always sums to 100% for each year. The main message is that the composition remains relatively balanced across the whole period, with all four components usually contributing around one quarter of the total. There is no strong long-term shift toward a single component, although some years show temporary dominance by Methane, Nitrous oxide, or Others.
03094.chart_structure: The chart type is a 100% stacked area chart. The variables represented are: - Period, shown as yearly categories from 2008 to 2025. - Percentage contribution, shown for four series: CO₂, Methane, Nitrous oxide, and Others. The X axis represents Period, covering 18 annual categories from 2008 through 2025. The Y axis represents % contribution, ranging from 0% to 100%. Because this is a 100% stacked chart, the four series together make up 100% in every year.
03094.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: A first important pattern is the overall balance of the four components. In most years, each category stays close to 25%, so the composition is generally even rather than highly concentrated in one source. A second pattern is that Methane is, on average, the largest contributor across the full period, with an average share of about 26.0%. Nitrous oxide follows at about 25.4%, Others at about 24.5%, and CO₂ is the lowest on average at about 24.1%. These differences are modest, reinforcing the idea of a fairly stable distribution. A third pattern is that short-term fluctuations matter more than long-term trend. Nitrous oxide leads in some years such as 2009 and 2013, Methane peaks strongly in 2017 and remains high again in 2023 to 2025, while Others becomes especially prominent in 2019 and 2021. By contrast, 2010, 2011, and 2016 are especially even years, with very small differences between the four shares.

Nitrous oxide ranges from 19.9% to 30.9%, with an average of 25.4%. Others ranges from 19.5% to 32.5%, with an average of 24.5%. Looking at notable yearly milestones, the most even composition occurs in 2016, where all four values lie between 23.8% and 25.6%, and similarly in 2010 and 2011, where the yearly ranges are only 2.5 and 2.0 percentage points. The most uneven years include 2021, when Others rises to 32.5%, 2019, when Others reaches 31.5%, 2017, when Methane reaches 31.2%, and 2009, when Nitrous oxide reaches 30.9%. 03111.essential_key_details: The maximum value in the chart is Renewable in Q4 at 56.6%, and the minimum value is Baseload in Q4 at 43.4%. 03120.overview_and_main_message: This scatter plot shows the relationship between two demographic indicators: population density and annual growth rate. Its purpose is to reveal whether these indicators move together and whether there are distinct clusters. The main message is a very strong negative relationship: places with lower density tend to have much higher annual growth, while places with higher density tend to have low or even negative growth. The data also suggest a few broad groupings along this downward pattern rather than a random spread.
03120.chart_structure: The chart type is a scatter plot with only markers, representing 24 observations from a single group. The horizontal axis shows **Density (inhabitants/km²)**, ranging from **40.52** to **569.54 inhabitants per square kilometre**. The vertical axis shows **Annual growth (%)**, ranging from **-0.83%** to **2.82%**. 03161.overview_and_main_message: This chart shows the relationship between two climate indicators: average temperature and per-capita emissions. Its purpose is to help determine whether warmer average temperatures are associated with higher or lower emissions. The main message is that there is essentially no meaningful relationship between the two variables: emissions vary widely across almost the full temperature range, so higher temperature does not consistently correspond to either higher or lower per-capita emissions.
03161.chart_structure: The chart is a scatter plot with markers representing individual observations. It displays one group of 40 observations. The X-axis represents average temperature, measured in degrees Celsius, ranging from 10.61°C to 27.61°C. The Y-axis represents per-capita emissions, measured in tonnes of CO2 equivalent, ranging from 2.66 to 13.61 tCO2e. Each point pairs one temperature value with one emissions value, allowing comparison of how the two quantitative variables move together, or fail to do so.
03161.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The dominant pattern is the absence of correlation. The reported correlation is about -0.06, which is extremely close to zero, and the linear trend is nearly flat. This indicates no meaningful positive or negative association between temperature and emissions. A second important pattern is broad vertical spread across many temperature values. Similar temperatures can be associated with very different emissions levels. For example, temperatures in the low to mid-20s °C include observations near the bottom of the emissions range as well as values above 11 and even above 13 tCO2e. A third pattern is that both low-temperature and high-temperature observations include a mix of moderate, low, and high emissions. This reinforces that variability in emissions is not explained by temperature alone in this dataset.
03161.essential_key_details: There are 40 observations in total. Average temperature spans from a minimum of 10.61°C to a maximum of 27.61°C. Per-capita emissions range from a minimum of 2.66 tCO2e to a maximum of 13.61 tCO2e, giving a spread of 10.95 tCO2e. The average emissions value is 7.82 tCO2e, and the median is 7.71 tCO2e. The highest emissions value, 13.61 tCO2e, occurs at 17.98°C. Another very high value is 13.49 tCO2e at 23.21°C. The lowest emissions value, 2.66 tCO2e, occurs at 21.32°C. Low values also appear at both cooler and warmer temperatures, including 2.94 tCO2e at 13.21°C and 24.98°C. These examples help show why the chart’s key message is no clear relationship between temperature and per-capita emissions.

03209.overview_and_main_message: This chart shows the relationship between two climate indicators: average temperature and per-capita emissions. Its purpose is to assess whether emissions tend to rise or fall as temperature changes, and whether that relationship is linear or curved. The main message is that there is no strong relationship: emissions vary widely across almost the full temperature range, and any overall upward tendency is weak.
03209.chart_structure: This is a scatter plot with only markers, containing 32 observations from a single group. Each point represents one paired measurement. The horizontal axis represents average temperature in degrees Celsius, ranging from 10.45°C to 27.4°C. The vertical axis represents per-capita emissions in tonnes of CO₂ equivalent, ranging from 2.51 to 13.54 tCO₂e. The chart therefore compares how per-capita emissions change, if at all, across different levels of average temperature.
03209.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: First, the data do not form a clear linear pattern. The reported correlation is low, about 0.27, and the overall linear trend is very small, which indicates only a slight positive association between temperature and emissions. Second, emissions are highly variable at both lower and higher temperatures. Lower temperatures include both some of the highest emissions and some low-to-mid values, while higher temperatures also include both low emissions and very high emissions. This broad spread means temperature alone does not explain emissions well in this sample. Third, many observations cluster around mid-range emissions rather than at the extremes. Values around roughly 8 to 10 tCO₂e appear common across a wide span of temperatures, reinforcing the impression of a scattered cloud rather than a strong upward or downward pattern.
03209.essential_key_details: Per-capita emissions range from a minimum of 2.51 tCO₂e at 21.97°C to a maximum of 13.54 tCO₂e at 10.45°C. The average emissions value is 7.94 tCO₂e, and the median is 8.045 tCO₂e, so a typical observation is close to 8 tCO₂e. The temperature axis spans from 10.45°C to 27.4°C. High-emission observations occur at both relatively low and relatively high temperatures, including 13.37 tCO₂e at 22.91°C and 12.95 tCO₂e at 24.74°C, while low-emission observations also occur in the middle and lower parts of the temperature range, such as 2.56 tCO₂e at 11.68°C and 2.65 tCO₂e at 15.75°C. These examples help explain why the chart’s main message is weak association rather than a clear temperature-emissions pattern.

Group 2 combines longer waiting times with higher resolved-case percentages, mostly from the upper 70s to the mid-90s. This separation makes the two groups substantially different from each other. 03292.overview_and_main_message: This chart is a scatter plot showing the relationship between two energy indicators: installed capacity and annual production. Its purpose is to compare individual observations and reveal whether higher installed capacity is generally associated with higher annual production. The main message is that there is a moderate positive relationship overall, but the data are highly variable and include one especially prominent outlier with both the highest capacity and the highest production.
03292.chart_structure: The chart type is a scatter plot with individual markers only, representing 24 observations in a single group. The horizontal axis represents Installed capacity, measured in megawatts (MW). It ranges from 35.09 MW to 1176.0 MW. The vertical axis represents Annual production, measured in gigawatt-hours (GWh). It ranges from 141.72 GWh to 6370.0 GWh. Each point corresponds to one observation pairing an installed-capacity value with an annual-production value, allowing comparison of how the two variables relate.
03292.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The first important pattern is an overall positive association: observations with larger installed capacity often also have higher annual production. The reported correlation is 0.557587, indicating a moderate relationship rather than a tight linear fit. The second pattern is substantial dispersion among observations with similar capacities. Around the mid-capacity range, production varies widely. For example, capacities around roughly 530 to 637 MW are linked to production values ranging from as low as 141.72 GWh to around 3790.63 GWh. This means capacity alone does not explain production consistently. The third pattern is the presence of a clear outlier. One observation at 1176.0 MW and 6370.0 GWh stands apart from the rest as the maximum on both axes, making it the most distinctive point in the chart.
03292.essential_key_details: The maximum installed capacity is 1176.0 MW, and it coincides with the maximum annual production of 6370.0 GWh. This annual production value is also identified as the single outlier. The minimum installed capacity is 35.09 MW, paired with 571.67 GWh. The minimum annual production is 141.72 GWh, occurring at an installed capacity of 530.59 MW, which is notable because it is far below many other observations with similar or even lower capacity. Across all 24 observations, the average annual production is 2044.83 GWh, with a median of 1558.53 GWh. The wide spread, reflected in a range of 6228.28 GWh and a standard deviation of 1484.93 GWh, reinforces that annual production varies considerably even when installed capacity is similar.

03467.overview_and_main_message: This chart shows the relationship between two energy indicators: installed capacity and annual production. Its purpose is to help judge whether the relationship is linear or curved. Overall, the chart suggests only a weak-to-moderate positive relationship rather than a tight straight-line pattern: annual production often increases as installed capacity increases, but the values are widely scattered, and one very high-production point stands out as a clear outlier. This means installed capacity alone does not explain production consistently across the sample.
03467.chart_structure: The chart is a scatter plot with smooth connecting lines and markers, containing a single series of 24 observations. 03467.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: First, the overall association is positive but not strong. The reported x-y correlation is 0.435, which indicates that higher installed capacity tends to be associated with higher annual production, but with substantial variation. For example, around the middle of the capacity range, production can be very low in one case and above 3000 GWh in others, showing that similar installed capacity can correspond to very different output levels. Third, the chart contains a clear outlier at the highest production level: 6370.0 GWh at 1176.0 MW. There is also a notable low-capacity, high-production case at 67.54 MW with 3860.69 GWh, reinforcing that the pattern is irregular rather than smoothly proportional.

Its purpose is to show how energy intensity changes across combinations of X and Y values and, in particular, to help identify the minimum valley of the surface. The X axis is labeled “X Axis” and runs from 1 to 6 in steps of 1. The Y axis is labeled “Y Axis” and also runs from 1 to 6 in steps of 1. The response variable is intensity, with values ranging from 10.2 to 47.1 across all grid points.
03925.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The strongest overall pattern is a downward movement in intensity from lower X and Y values toward higher X and Y values. Early grid positions have many values in the 30s and 40s, while the lowest region is found where both coordinates are relatively large. A clear minimum valley appears in the upper end of Y combined with mid-to-high X values. The deepest point is at X=4, Y=6, and nearby low values include X=4, Y=5 at 11.4 and X=3, Y=6 at 14.5, indicating that the low-intensity zone is a cluster rather than a single isolated point. The surface is not perfectly smooth, because there are local fluctuations. For example, some values rise slightly instead of continuing to fall, such as from X=4, Y=6 at 10.2 to X=5, Y=6 at 17.9, and from X=5, Y=1 at 29.4 to X=6, Y=1 at 32.9. Even with these irregularities, the dominant pattern remains a general decline toward the high-X, high-Y region.
03925.essential_key_details: The maximum intensity is 47.1 at X=1, Y=1. The minimum intensity is 10.2 at X=4, Y=6. The full intensity range is therefore 36.9 units. This average sits well above the values in the minimum valley, confirming that the region around X=4 to 6 and Y=5 to 6 is substantially lower than the typical level across the surface. The axes themselves both span from 1 to 6, with a midpoint average of 3.5 on each axis, so the lowest-energy area occurs beyond the midpoint on both dimensions rather than near the center.

04042.overview_and_main_message: This chart is a filled radar chart comparing education indicator scores for three school sectors: Public, State-funded private, and Private. Its purpose is to show the compared profile of education indicators and whether performance is balanced across subjects or dominated by a few indicators. The main message is that Mathematics and Reading are the strongest areas overall, while Science and especially Digital skills are weaker. Public schools have the most even profile, whereas Private schools show the sharpest drop from core academic subjects to Science and Digital skills.
04042.chart_structure: The chart type is a filled radar chart with multiple series plotted on common axes. The variables represented are school sector and education indicator score. 04042.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: First, the overall profile is stronger in Mathematics and Reading than in the other two indicators. Average scores by indicator are about 64.6 in Mathematics and 64.3 in Reading, compared with 60.6 in Science and 57.1 in Digital skills. This shows a clear shift downward from literacy and numeracy toward Science and especially Digital skills. Second, Public schools are the most balanced across indicators. Their scores stay within a narrow range from 60.8 to 63.9, with an average of 62.85. By contrast, State-funded private schools vary more, from 57.5 to 66.2, and Private schools vary the most, from 53.0 to 64.8, indicating a less even profile. Third, the leading sector changes by indicator. State-funded private schools have the highest scores in Mathematics at 65.6 and Reading at 66.2, Public schools lead Science at 63.9 and also Digital skills at 60.8, while Private schools do not lead any indicator and fall notably behind in Science and Digital skills.

Digital skills has the lowest average at 57.1. By series, Public and State-funded private are very similar on average, at 62.85 and 62.75 respectively, while Private is lower at 59.38. These values confirm that the chart communicates a broadly similar but not identical profile across sectors, with the clearest weakness concentrated in Digital skills and the greatest imbalance in the Private sector.

04739.overview_and_main_message: This chart shows the evolution of web analytics over the period 2014 to 2025 using two related measures: monthly sessions and conversion rate. Its main message is that web traffic grows strongly and steadily across the whole period, while the conversion rate remains almost unchanged at about 26%, implying that the increase in conversions would mainly come from higher traffic rather than from improved conversion efficiency.
04739.chart_structure: This is a combo chart that combines clustered columns with a line and uses a secondary axis. The horizontal axis represents Period, with yearly categories from 2014 through 2025. The primary vertical axis represents Monthly sessions (thousands). The primary series corresponds to monthly sessions. The secondary vertical axis represents Conversion (%). The secondary series corresponds to conversion rate.
04739.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The clearest pattern is sustained growth in the primary series. Monthly sessions rise from 138.3 thousand in 2014 to 358.3 thousand in 2025, with no yearly declines, indicating a strong long-term increase in traffic. A second pattern is the remarkable stability of the secondary series. Conversion stays within a very narrow band from 25.9% to 26.4% across all years, so there is almost no meaningful upward or downward trend in that metric. A third important comparison is that the two series behave differently over time: sessions change substantially, while conversion barely changes. This means the chart communicates growth in volume rather than growth in conversion performance.
04739.essential_key_details: For monthly sessions, the minimum value is 138.3 thousand in 2014 and the maximum is 358.3 thousand in 2025. Key milestones in the traffic series include passing 200 thousand in 2017 with 205.1 thousand, exceeding 300 thousand in 2023 with 311.5 thousand, and reaching the period peak in 2025. The conversion series does not show comparable milestones because it remains essentially flat throughout.

04779.chart: Evolution of web analytics by period (04779)

04779.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The primary series, monthly sessions, shows a strong long-term upward trend. 04807.chart_structure: The chart is a combo chart, specifically clustered columns plus a line with a secondary axis. 04807.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The first and clearest pattern is strong growth in the primary series. The second pattern is the stability of the secondary series. Pool price fluctuates only slightly between 25.9 and 26.5 €/MWh across all years, indicating almost no meaningful change compared with the strong upward movement in generation. The third pattern is the contrast between the two series. The chart’s communicative purpose is to show that the secondary-axis series does not mirror the strong expansion of generation. While generation climbs rapidly, pool price remains essentially constant, so the two measures evolve very differently over the same period.
04807.essential_key_details: For the primary series, the minimum value is 675.8 GWh in 2017, the maximum is 2333.5 GWh in 2025, and the average across the nine periods is about 1482.2 GWh. This very narrow range of just 0.6 €/MWh confirms that pool price is broadly stable throughout the period.

04968.chart: Evolution of web analytics by period (04968)
04968.overview_and_main_message: This combo chart shows the evolution of web analytics from 2014 to 2025, combining monthly sessions on a primary axis with conversion rate on a secondary axis. Its main message is that web traffic grows strongly over the period, while conversion remains almost unchanged at about 26%, indicating that the increase in overall performance is driven mainly by higher session volume rather than by improving conversion efficiency.
04968.chart_structure: The chart is a temporal combo chart with two series and a secondary vertical axis. The horizontal axis represents Period, with yearly categories from 2014 through 2025. The primary vertical axis represents Monthly sessions, measured in thousands. The secondary vertical axis represents Conversion, measured as a percentage. The Primary series is plotted against the monthly sessions axis and records yearly values from 108.7 thousand sessions in 2014 to 398.7 thousand in 2025. The Secondary series is plotted against the conversion axis and stays within a very narrow range, from 25.9% to 26.5%, across the same years.
04968.relevant_patterns_trends_and_comparisons: The dominant pattern is sustained growth in the Primary series. Monthly sessions rise from 108.7 thousand in 2014 to 398.7 thousand in 2025, with only one slight interruption: a small dip from 366.7 thousand in 2023 to 366.2 thousand in 2024 before reaching a new peak in 2025. A second important pattern is the remarkable stability of the Secondary series. Conversion fluctuates only slightly between 25.9% and 26.5% over the entire period, showing no meaningful upward or downward trend. Together, these two patterns suggest that the chart’s secondary axis is essential for interpretation: despite very strong traffic growth, conversion performance remains essentially flat. This means the web analytics improvement over time is concentrated in acquiring more sessions rather than increasing the proportion that converts.
04968.essential_key_details: For monthly sessions, the minimum is 108.7 thousand in 2014, the maximum is 398.7 thousand in 2025, and the average across the period is about 256.7 thousand. A notable milestone is the crossing of 300 thousand sessions in 2021, when the value reaches 310.0 thousand. For conversion, the minimum is 25.9% in 2014, the maximum is 26.5% in 2015 and again in 2025, and the average is about 26.2%. The total variation is only 0.6 percentage points, reinforcing that conversion is highly stable throughout the period.
